stem.en: You have 4 g of hydrogen and 16 g of oxygen. You combine them into water. What is left over?

text.en: 2 g of hydrogen. Water needs 1 g of hydrogen per 8 g of oxygen, so 16 g of oxygen uses only 2 g.

feedback.en: 4 to 16 is 1 to 4. Water is 1 to 8. Half the hydrogen has no oxygen to join.
All 16 g of oxygen get used, because 2 g of hydrogen is enough to take all of it. It is hydrogen that is in excess.

text.en: It depends on how hot you make it.

feedback.en: Heat changes how fast the joining happens, never the recipe. Grains join in whole numbers at any temperature.

explanation.en: Divide the oxygen by 8 to find how much hydrogen it can take. 16 divided by 8 is 2. You had 4. Two grams stay behind.
